summary: Starting in December 2026, new jobs compute created in the UI will default to Auto access mode in workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled. Auto uses Standard access mode unless a machine learning runtime, a GPU instance type, or a Databricks Runtime version lower than 14.3 is selected. A cluster policy that enforces a different access mode still takes precedence. Existing jobs are not changed. See Use standard access mode.
title: New jobs compute will soon default to Auto access mode for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled

summary: Admins can use ug configure --global from their mobile device management (MDM) software to provision the Claude desktop app machine-wide with governed models, MCP servers, and skills, and users can import their claude.ai projects and chats. This is available on macOS only. Learn more.
title: Provision Claude desktop with MDM using Unity Gateway

summary: Bug fixes Fix real-time mode reservation liveness and occupied-slot accounting when tasks execute through Aether.
title: Databricks Runtime 19: November 9, 2026

summary: Dynamic value references in Lakeflow Jobs can now shift a date by a duration before formatting it. For example, {{(job.start_time - 1.day).iso_date}} passes the date of the day before the run started to a task. Date arithmetic is in Beta. See Shift dates with date arithmetic.
title: Shift dates in Lakeflow Jobs parameters with date arithmetic (Beta)

summary: Admins can use ug configure --global from their mobile device management (MDM) software to provision the Claude desktop app machine-wide with governed models, MCP servers, and skills, and users can import their claude.ai projects and chats. This is available on macOS only. Learn more.
title: Provision Claude desktop with MDM using Unity Gateway

summary: When you create new jobs compute in the UI, the access mode now defaults to Auto instead of Dedicated. Auto uses Standard access mode unless a machine learning runtime, a GPU instance type, or a Databricks Runtime version lower than 14.3 is selected. A cluster policy that enforces a different access mode still takes precedence. Existing jobs are not changed. For workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled, this change takes effect in December 2026. See What's coming. See Use standard access mode.
title: New jobs compute defaults to Auto access mode

summary: Genie Search is now generally available. Genie Search indexes your organization's knowledge in sources such as Google Drive, Jira, Confluence, and Workday, so Genie One can search all of that knowledge in one place. Azure Databricks indexes each document's permissions with its content and keeps both current, so users see only the documents that they can already access in the source. Genie Search also powers the following features in Genie One: Org directories: Find teammates, browse the org chart, and view profiles from Workday. See Browse org directories in Genie One. Search in Discover: Search Azure Databricks assets and content from connected sources in one place. See Use Genie Search in Genie One. Databricks recommends using Genie Search together with MCP connectors, which let Genie One access live data and take action in the applications your team uses.
title: Genie Search is now generally available

summary: Genie Ontology is now generally available. Genie Ontology is the context layer that gives Genie One, Genie Code, and other AI agents a business-aware map of your organization. It combines modeled knowledge that you define in Unity Catalog semantics with learned knowledge that Genie extracts from your assets and usage.
title: Genie Ontology is now generally available

summary: The Databricks Genie app in Microsoft Teams is now generally available. Chat with the app in a direct message or mention @Databricks Genie in a channel or group chat to get answers to data questions without leaving Microsoft Teams. See Databricks Genie app in Microsoft Teams.
title: Databricks Genie app in Microsoft Teams is now generally available

summary: The Databricks Genie app for Slack is now generally available. Send a direct message to the app or mention @Genie in a channel or group DM to get answers to data questions without leaving Slack. See Databricks Genie app for Slack.
title: Databricks Genie app for Slack is now generally available

summary: You can now recover a dropped Unity Catalog volume within 7 days. Find its ID with SHOW VOLUMES DROPPED, then run UNDROP VOLUME WITH ID to restore it with its privileges and tags. Requires Databricks Runtime 19 and above. See UNDROP VOLUME.
title: Recover dropped Unity Catalog volumes with UNDROP VOLUME

summary: Zhipu AI GLM 5.2 is deprecated and will be retired on February 4, 2027. GLM 5.3 is the recommended replacement. See Legacy, deprecated, and retired models for migration guidance.
title: Zhipu AI GLM 5.2 is scheduled for retirement

summary: Unity Catalog wikis are in Beta. A wiki lets your team document a table's meaning, intended use, and sources, then collaborate on that information. Data owners and stewards draft and publish wikis in Catalog Explorer, manually or with Genie Code, and anyone who can view the table's metadata can comment on, suggest edits to, and react to published wikis. Account admins can control access to this feature from the Previews page.
title: Unity Catalog wikis are in Beta

summary: Account admins can now restore a deleted Unity Catalog metastore by its ID. You can restore a metastore for up to 5 days after it's deleted. See Restore a deleted metastore.
title: Restore a deleted Unity Catalog metastore with the REST API (Public Preview)

summary: UCDataset streams rows from Unity Catalog tables directly into PyTorch training loops on AI Runtime, without Spark or a SQL warehouse. It applies filter expressions and deletion vectors as it reads, and splits the matching rows across GPUs and data loader workers. See Load Unity Catalog tables into PyTorch with UCDataset.
title: Load Unity Catalog tables into PyTorch on AI Runtime (Beta)

summary: You can now install the JDBC driver for a JDBC Unity Catalog connection from a Maven coordinate instead of uploading it to a volume. This requires serverless compute, Databricks Runtime 19 or above, or SQL warehouses 2026.43 or above. See Maven coordinates.
title: Install drivers for JDBC Unity Catalog connections from Maven

summary: Azure Databricks plans to support Tableau and Sigma as external knowledge sources. See External knowledge sources.
title: More external knowledge sources

summary: Smart Routing now routes only subagents, not the first prompt. It costs up to 70% less in internal benchmarks and cuts p90 routing latency from 9 seconds to 2 seconds. Smart Routing for Codex is paused. See Select models or use Smart Routing.
title: Smart Routing is faster and lower cost, and now routes subagents only (Beta)

summary: Starting in January 2027, AI Functions in SQL queries will no longer be supported on Databricks Runtime versions below 17.3 LTS. This change doesn't affect ai_similarity or the AI Functions REST API. To continue using AI Functions in SQL, use Databricks Runtime 17.3 LTS and above.
title: Upcoming removal of AI Functions support on older runtimes

summary: Smart Routing now routes only subagents, not the first prompt. It costs up to 70% less in internal benchmarks and cuts p90 routing latency from 9 seconds to 2 seconds. Smart Routing for Codex is paused. See Select models or use Smart Routing.
title: Smart Routing is faster and lower cost, and now routes subagents only (Beta)

summary: Claude Code and Codex are now available in SSH tunnel sessions. The agents send model requests through Unity Gateway and authenticate with the credentials of your SSH session. This requires Databricks CLI version 1.23.0 or above. See Run coding agents in an SSH session.
title: Run Claude Code and Codex in the SSH tunnel

summary: Providers can publish governed business metrics in Databricks Marketplace by adding metric views. Only Azure Databricks recipients can use shared metric views. See Create a Marketplace listing and Add metric views to a share.
title: Metric view listings are generally available in Databricks Marketplace

summary: Azure Databricks is a FedRAMP® Authorized Cloud Service Offering (CSO) at the high impact level in the Azure East US and East US2 (commercial) regions. To process data regulated by FedRAMP High, enable the compliance security profile on your workspace and select the FedRAMP High compliance standard. Serverless compute workloads require base environment version 5 or higher. See FedRAMP High.
title: FedRAMP High compliance controls now available on Azure Databricks on Azure

summary: External knowledge sources are in Beta. You can pull metadata from Power BI semantic models into Azure Databricks, and Genie can use your Power BI measure definitions when it answers questions. To use external knowledge sources, an account admin turns on External knowledge from the account console Previews page. See Manage account-level previews.
title: External knowledge sources are in Beta

summary: DeepSeek V4 Flash (0731) is retired as of November 5, 2026. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (1017) is the recommended replacement. See Legacy, deprecated, and retired models for migration guidance.
title: DeepSeek V4 Flash (0731) is retired

summary: Context-based ingress policies can now allow traffic from Power BI, Tableau Cloud, dbt Cloud, and the Genie apps for Slack and Microsoft Teams. Azure Databricks keeps partner details current, so you don't track IPs. See Allow partner platforms in context-based ingress policies.

summary: You can now upload Markdown (.md) and text (.txt) files to a Genie One conversation and ask questions about their contents. See Upload a file.
title: Upload Markdown and text files

summary: Genie Code and Genie One turns can now be exported to the Unity Gateway unified trace table as OpenTelemetry spans. A workspace admin turns on tracing for each product from the Previews page. By default, only the trace table's owner can query the traces. See Monitor Genie Code and Genie One with the unified trace table.

summary: Genie One now responds more quickly when you ask a question.
title: Faster responses

summary: You can now open a visualization from a Genie One response in the side panel, where you can interact with it at a larger size next to the conversation. See Expand a visualization.
title: Expand visualizations

summary: Benchmark questions now run in parallel, so benchmark evaluations finish sooner. See Benchmarks.
title: Faster benchmark runs

summary: For Genie Agents that an app queries with an OAuth custom identity claim, the Monitor tab can now show each message's claim, so you can tell which of the app's end users asked it. Turn on the Custom claim column from the column picker. See Monitor the agent.
title: Custom claims in the Monitor tab

summary: Users who can access only some of the volumes or MCP connections attached to a Genie Agent are no longer blocked from using it. The agent answers using only the sources that the user can access. See Manage data objects.
title: Answers from accessible sources

summary: Labels on waterfall charts now stay visible when they're close to the top or bottom of the axis.
title: Waterfall chart labels

summary: Authors can now reorder dashboard variables directly in the dashboard editor. See Use dashboard variables.
title: Reorder dashboard variables

summary: Genie Code for dashboard authoring can now import the relationships declared on Unity Catalog metric views into a dashboard as dashboard relationships. See Use relationships with Genie Code for dashboard authoring.
title: Import relationships from Unity Catalog with Genie Code (Beta)

summary: Authors can now set a display name for each option in a field variable, such as Total revenue instead of Sum of sales. You can also ask Genie Code to set, rename, or clear these display names, and it keeps the names you set when it edits the variable. See Set display names for field options.
title: Display names for field variable options

summary: Beginning in January 2027, AI Functions that require Databricks Runtime 15.4 LTS or above, other than ai_similarity, require Databricks Runtime 17.3 LTS or above. Calls to these functions on Databricks Runtime versions below 17.3 are no longer supported and return an error. Upgrade the compute that runs affected SQL queries to Databricks Runtime 17.3 LTS or above before support ends. This change does not affect the AI Functions REST API. See Transform unstructured data using AI Functions.

summary: Publish Git-managed skills to Unity Catalog with a GitHub Action in Beta. Map folders to skills and publish updates on merges to your publishing branch. See Publish skills from your GitHub repository.

summary: Publish Git-managed skills to Unity Catalog with a GitHub Action in Beta. Map folders to skills and publish updates on merges to your publishing branch. See Publish skills from your GitHub repository.

summary: You can now add AI Function tasks to your Azure Databricks jobs to run ai_parse_document, ai_extract, or ai_classify on the files in a volume or the rows of a table, without writing SQL. Each run processes only the inputs that are new or changed since the previous run and writes the results to a Unity Catalog table that later tasks can read. This feature is in Beta. See AI Function tasks for jobs.
title: AI Function tasks for jobs (Beta)

summary: Databricks SQL version 2026.45 is now available in the Preview channel. Review the following section to learn about new features. Share views with or without history ALTER SHARE... ADD VIEW and ALTER SHARE... ALTER VIEW now accept the WITH HISTORY and WITHOUT HISTORY clauses. Existing history defaults are unchanged.

summary: Write Lakeflow Designer results to Google Drive or SharePoint with the Output operator. Each run creates or replaces a file of up to 2.75 MiB. See Output.
title: Write Lakeflow Designer results to Google Drive or SharePoint

summary: You can now run a Lakeflow Job when one or more upstream jobs complete, including across workspaces attached to the same Unity Catalog metastore. Configure dependencies on the downstream job. See Trigger jobs when upstream jobs complete.
title: Trigger Lakeflow Jobs when upstream jobs complete (Beta)

summary: Start a visual data prep in Lakeflow Designer from suggested, favorite, or recently used tables on the welcome screen. See Browse existing tables.

summary: Set checkpoint options across a visual data prep file with Set all to Auto or Set all to On. See Configure operator checkpoints.

summary: The managed Okta connector is now available in Beta in Databricks Lakeflow Connect. Workspace admins can enable Lakeflow Connect for Okta on the Previews page. Use the connector to ingest identity and access data from Okta into Azure Databricks, including users, groups, group memberships, app integrations, devices, policies, and administrator roles. The connector uses SSWS API token authentication and supports incremental ingestion.
title: Okta connector is available in Beta

summary: You can now run read queries on tables protected by row filters, column masks, and attribute-based access control (ABAC) policies with Lakehouse//RT. See Fine-grained access control.

summary: Use Genie Code in Lakeflow Designer to create shared custom operators or edit them by workspace YAML file path. See Build a shared custom operator.
title: Edit shared Lakeflow Designer operators with Genie Code

summary: When you write to Lakebase from Structured Streaming, you can use merge strategies to control how upserts update individual columns. Keep the first or last value, ignore nulls, or select values by an ordering column. Merge strategies require Databricks Runtime 19 and above. See Merge strategies for upserts.
title: Control Lakebase sink upserts with merge strategies

summary: When Genie needs approval to run a connected external tool, the Databricks Genie apps for Slack and Microsoft Teams now show an approval prompt in the reply, so you can allow or deny the action without leaving the chat. See Approve tool actions and Approve tool actions.
title: Approve Genie tool actions in Slack and Microsoft Teams (Public Preview)

summary: New features and improvements ALTER SHARE ADD/ALTER VIEW now accepts WITH HISTORY and WITHOUT HISTORY; existing history defaults are unchanged. Library and environment updates Updated Python libraries: pytz from 2025.2 to 2026.5 tzdata from 2026.2 to 2026.5

summary: Ingesting into tables backed by default storage with Zerobus Ingest in Lakeflow Connect is now generally available. See Create or identify the target table.
title: Zerobus Ingest into default storage is now generally available

summary: Simba JDBC Driver (Legacy) 2.8.7 updates jackson-core, jackson-databind, and jackson-datatype-jsr310 to 2.21.8. Download it from the JDBC drivers archive under All JDBC Driver Versions (Simba).
title: Simba JDBC Driver (Legacy) 2.8.7 is available

summary: OneLake external locations are now in Public Preview. Use a OneLake external location as managed storage for a Unity Catalog catalog to store managed tables, volumes, materialized views, and streaming tables in Microsoft OneLake while Unity Catalog governs access. Workspace admins can control access to External location support for OneLake from the Previews page. See Connect Azure Databricks to a OneLake external location.
title: OneLake external locations are in Public Preview

summary: With managed warehouse, users can view traces stored in Unity Catalog in the MLflow UI without selecting a SQL warehouse. MLflow runs trace queries on a SQL warehouse that it creates in your workspace when your workspace supports it, and on serverless compute otherwise. Workspace admins can enable Managed Warehouse for MLflow on the Previews page. See Managed warehouse for MLflow traces.
title: Managed warehouse for MLflow (Beta)

summary: A schema can now hold up to 1,000 Unity Catalog secrets, and a metastore up to 10,000, up from 100 and 1,000. The limits apply to Azure Databricks-managed secrets and secrets backed by Azure Key Vault. BROWSE on a catalog now applies to Unity Catalog secrets, so users can discover secrets and their metadata without being able to read the values or reference the secrets in code. See Grant access to secrets.
title: Higher limits and BROWSE support for Unity Catalog secrets

summary: A Genie Agent can now analyze unstructured files stored in Unity Catalog volumes, such as PDFs, slide decks, and images, and answer with citations that point to the source page. Workspace admins can control access from the Previews page. See Analyze files in volumes with a Genie Agent.
title: Analyze files in Unity Catalog volumes (Public Preview)

summary: Beginning November 1, 2026, Unity Gateway budgets include spend from task-specific AI Functions such as ai_parse_document, ai_extract, and ai_classify across batch and real-time execution paths. See Manage budgets for Unity Gateway.
title: AI Functions usage is now included in Unity Gateway budgets

summary: Beginning November 1, 2026, Unity Gateway budgets include spend from task-specific AI Functions such as ai_parse_document, ai_extract, and ai_classify across batch and real-time execution paths. See Manage budgets for Unity Gateway.

summary: You can now use the Dsv7, Ddsv7, Esv7, Edsv7, and Famdsv7 series (4 to 32 vCPUs) and the 48, 64, and 80 vCPU sizes of the Lsv4 and Lasv4 series for classic compute. See Worker node type.

summary: You can now track usage of Unity Gateway Skills, which are in Beta. Audit logs record skill list, load, and file fetch events under the aiGatewaySkills service. The Skills tab of the usage dashboard shows downloads, loads, and activity by user.
title: Track Unity Gateway skill usage with audit logs and the usage dashboard

summary: Claude Code auto mode is now supported for both Anthropic and non-Anthropic models hosted by Azure Databricks. Auto mode reviews tool calls to reduce routine permission prompts. See Auto mode.
title: Claude Code auto mode for Anthropic and non-Anthropic models

summary: You can now track usage of Unity Gateway Skills, which are in Beta. Audit logs record skill list, load, and file fetch events under the aiGatewaySkills service. The Skills tab of the usage dashboard shows downloads, loads, and activity by user.
title: Track Unity Gateway skill usage with audit logs and the usage dashboard

summary: Thinking Machine Labs Inkling was retired on October 30, 2026. GLM 5.3 or Kimi K3 is the recommended replacement. See Legacy, deprecated, and retired models for migration guidance.
title: Thinking Machine Labs Inkling is retired

summary: Relationships between Unity Catalog metric views are in Beta. Use ALTER VIEW... ADD CONSTRAINT... RELATIONSHIP to record how a source metric view joins to a target metric view, including the cardinality and the join condition, so that AI assistants and BI tools choose the right join path. Relationships require Databricks Runtime 19 and above, or a SQL warehouse. See Relationships between metric views.
title: Relationships between metric views (Beta)

summary: Moonshot AI Kimi K2.7 was retired on October 30, 2026. Kimi K3 is the recommended replacement. See Legacy, deprecated, and retired models for migration guidance.
title: Moonshot AI Kimi K2.7 is retired

summary: You can now see how current each destination table is in Lakeflow Connect database connector pipelines, in Public Preview. The new Data freshness column in the pipeline's tables list shows the time since the latest source commit that the pipeline ingested for each change data capture (CDC) table. Data freshness is available for SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and Oracle sources. You can also query data freshness and end-to-end lag from the ingestion pipeline's event log, and create alerts on them. See Monitor data freshness for change data capture (CDC) tables.
title: Monitor data freshness in Lakeflow Connect database connector pipelines (Public Preview)

summary: The managed Microsoft Graph Logs connector is now available in Beta in Databricks Lakeflow Connect. Use the connector to ingest security alerts from Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Sentinel, and other Microsoft security products into Azure Databricks. The connector uses OAuth machine-to-machine authentication with a Microsoft Entra ID application and supports incremental ingestion.
title: Microsoft Graph Logs connector is available in Beta

summary: Claude Code auto mode is now supported for both Anthropic and non-Anthropic models hosted by Azure Databricks. Auto mode reviews tool calls to reduce routine permission prompts. See Auto mode.
title: Claude Code auto mode for Anthropic and non-Anthropic models

summary: Azure West US 2, South Central US, and Australia Southeast now each have a dedicated regional control plane. Before this release, West US 2 and South Central US workspaces used the West US-based control plane, and Australia Southeast workspaces used the Australia East-based control plane. New workspaces created in these regions use the regional control plane and require firewall allowlist entries for the new secure cluster connectivity (SCC) relay tunnel, Control Plane NAT IPs, Metastore, and Event Hubs endpoint. Australia Southeast adds a new Log Blob storage value. South Central US also adds an East US Artifact Blob storage secondary alongside the existing North Central US value. All South Central US workspaces should allowlist both. Existing workspaces continue to use their current control plane unless they migrate to the regional control plane. See IP addresses and domains for Azure Databricks services and assets.
title: Azure West US 2, South Central US, and Australia Southeast now have dedicated regional control planes

summary: Starting in December 2026, Databricks-provided MCP connectors in Genie One and Genie Code will be enabled by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled. The connectors include Google Drive, Gmail, Google Calendar, Microsoft 365, Atlassian, Slack, and GitHub. They let Genie One and Genie Code connect to third-party services to search your documents and data and take actions on your behalf. Azure Databricks governs each connection through Unity Catalog and Unity Gateway. See Databricks-provided MCPs, Connect Genie One to external applications with MCP, and Connect Genie Code to MCP servers.
title: Databricks-provided MCP connectors in Genie One and Genie Code will soon be enabled by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled

summary: The managed Xero connector is now available in Beta in Databricks Lakeflow Connect. Workspace admins can enable it from the Previews page. Use the connector to ingest accounting data such as invoices, payments, and contacts from Xero into Azure Databricks. The connector uses OAuth user authorization, ingests transaction tables such as invoices and payments incrementally, and removes deleted records for supported tables.
title: Xero connector is available in Beta

summary: Simba JDBC Driver (Legacy) 2.8.6 prevents pending Cloud Fetch downloads from delaying the last connection from closing. It also updates lz4-java, Jackson, and libthrift. Download it from the JDBC drivers archive under All JDBC Driver Versions (Simba).
title: Simba JDBC Driver (Legacy) 2.8.6 is available

summary: Real-time mode in Lakeflow pipelines is now generally available on classic compute and serverless compute. Use it for operational workloads that need end-to-end latency as low as five milliseconds, such as fraud detection. See Use real-time mode in Lakeflow pipelines.
title: Real-time mode in Lakeflow pipelines is now generally available

summary: Native XML file format support is now generally available. You can ingest, query, and parse XML files in batch or streaming workloads with Auto Loader, read_files, and COPY INTO, and use the from_xml and schema_of_xml SQL functions. See Read and write XML files.
title: Native XML file format support is now generally available

summary: Anomaly detection for data quality monitoring is now generally available. Enable it at the schema level to monitor the freshness and completeness of every table in the schema, based on historical data patterns. Results for all monitored tables are stored in the system.data_quality_monitoring.table_results system table, which is also now generally available. See Anomaly detection.
title: Data quality monitoring anomaly detection is now generally available

summary: You can now choose which workspace is billed for the hourly charges of Private Link endpoints and private network gateways in a network connectivity configuration (NCC). See Choose a billing workspace for private endpoint charges.
title: Choose a billing workspace for private endpoint charges (Public Preview)

summary: You can now apply attribute-based access control (ABAC) row filters and column masks to views, materialized views, and streaming tables shared through OpenSharing. Shared views are in Beta and require the ABAC on views preview. See OpenSharing and ABAC.
title: Apply ABAC policies to shared views, materialized views, and streaming tables

summary: Azure Databricks will soon start rejecting unpaginated requests to some Unity Catalog REST API operations, such as list catalogs, list schemas, and list tables, with HTTP 400 responses. Prior to this, unpaginated requests to these operations are subject to progressively stricter rate limits and will receive HTTP 429 responses, potentially causing jobs to run more slowly due to retries, or fail if the client does not handle these errors. The paginated forms of these operations remain available. If you call these operations directly, update your clients to set max_results=0 and follow with next_page_token until all pages are retrieved. If you use a Databricks SDK or the Databricks CLI, upgrade to a current release, which uses these fields by default. For the full list of affected operations and update instructions, see Paginate Unity Catalog REST API operations.
title: Unpaginated requests to some Unity Catalog REST API operations will soon be rejected

Account admins must still configure these features before they take effect. This includes features for network connectivity (such as private connectivity), network security (such as ingress and egress controls), encryption, and enhanced security and compliance. summary: Lakebase Insights now diagnoses issues using telemetry from the system.lakebase system tables and recommends next steps. The Lakebase Insights workspace preview enables automatic telemetry capture. Users with CAN MANAGE can configure Insights directly in each project's Settings, without creating an observability configuration. This preview was previously named Lakebase Advanced Postgres Telemetry. Workspaces that used Insights before already have it enabled. To set up Insights: If the preview isn't already enabled, ask a workspace admin to enable Lakebase Insights from the Previews page. Insights needs telemetry in system.lakebase to analyze a project, so enabling the Insights preview also enables Lakebase Observability in System Tables if it isn't already enabled. Workspace admins can enable the observability preview separately to capture telemetry without Insights. To schedule Insights runs for a project, you need CAN MANAGE on that project. Enable Insights and set its analysis frequency in Settings. You can run Insights on demand at any time, with or without a schedule. If you scheduled Insights through an observability configuration, those jobs have stopped. Their schedules do not carry over. Those configurations no longer write telemetry to their Unity Catalog destinations, so their dashboards retain historical data but receive no new data. To continue receiving scheduled insights, enable Insights and set an analysis frequency in each project's Settings. Each project runs separately, and each run uses compute and model tokens, so choose which projects to analyze and how often. Insights remains in Beta. See Detect issues with Insights.
title: Lakebase Insights moves to per-project settings, with on-demand runs (Beta)

summary: Starting December 2, 2026, CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW will update views in-place, instead of dropping and re-creating the view. Grants, tags, and comments are preserved with one caveat: You must first remove governed tags on a view column before dropping the column via CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW. Otherwise, the statement will fail with a CANNOT_DROP_TAGGED_COLUMN error to protect the ABAC policies that depend on them (learn more). Use CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW <catalog>.<schema>.<view> NOCOPY * … to drop grants, tags and comments on view explicitly (governed tags are still retained). See CREATE VIEW and Upcoming change to CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW metadata preservation.

summary: The new lakebase_tokenizer extension lets you control how Lakebase Search turns text into search terms, so keyword search matches the way your data and users actually read. Native PostgreSQL full-text search gives you little control over this step. lakebase_tokenizer adds a configurable whole-word tokenizer through PostgreSQL's standard text-search dictionary interface, with the controls that matter for relevance: Normalization: lowercase text, apply Unicode normalization for byte-stable matching, and strip accents so café matches cafe. Stopwords and synonyms: manage your own stopword and synonym lists in SQL, so terms like usa and united_states match the same rows. Stemming and possessives: reduce words to their root with a native English stemmer and strip trailing 's, so running matches run and John's matches john. It produces standard tsvector values, so a tokenizer you configure works with to_tsvector, GIN (generalized inverted index) indexes, and the lakebase_text lakebase_bm25 index for BM25 (best match 25) ranking. Install it after enabling Lakebase Search in your project settings. See lakebase_tokenizer.
title: Lakebase Search adds a configurable text tokenizer for keyword search

summary: Lakebase Search is now generally available. It brings scalable vector and keyword search to Lakebase projects through two Postgres extensions, so you can run semantic and exact-term search in a single database without a separate search stack: lakebase_vector adds the lakebase_ann index type for approximate nearest-neighbor vector search. It is drop-in compatible with pgvector, using the same types, operators, and query syntax, and scales to over 1 billion vectors on a single index with builds up to 50-100x faster than HNSW. lakebase_text adds the lakebase_bm25 index type for BM25 full-text search. It works with standard tsvector types and operators, adding BM25 ranking and top-K pushdown that PostgreSQL's native GIN index does not provide. Indexes are storage-backed, so they are available immediately after scale-to-zero without warmup. Combine both extensions for hybrid search that returns semantic and exact-term matches in one ranked list. To get started, enable Lakebase Search in your project settings, then install the extensions. See Lakebase Search, lakebase_vector, and lakebase_text.
title: Lakebase Search is generally available

summary: The preset theme picker now shows a color palette preview for each theme before you select it.
title: Theme picker previews

summary: You can now style the headers and values of a pivot table's totals independently, and apply conditional styling to them. See Style pivot table totals.
title: Style pivot table totals

summary: Genie Code for dashboard authoring now understands SQL dataset parameters when building and editing dashboards. See Use Genie Code for dashboard authoring.
title: SQL dataset parameters in Genie Code

summary: You can now reorder the options in a field variable.
title: Reorder field variable options

summary: Type @ in a visualization widget's title or description to insert a field reference. The reference shows a live, formatted metric, such as a sum or an average, that responds to the dashboard's filters. Click the reference to change the field, aggregation function, and number or date formatting. See Reference a filter or a field.
title: Reference aggregated field values in widget titles and descriptions

summary: You can now scale a numeric axis to each subchart's own data on a faceted chart instead of sharing one range across subcharts. Set the axis range to Per facet. See Faceting.

summary: You can now set the number of row and column hierarchy levels a pivot table expands to when it first loads. See Set the default expand level.

summary: Fixed a bug where undo and redo did not apply to dashboard variables.
title: Dashboard variable undo and redo fix

summary: You can now convert a SQL dataset into a local metric view from the dataset's context menu, and Genie Code handles the conversion. See Local metric views and Use Genie Code for dashboard authoring.
title: Convert a SQL dataset to a local metric view

summary: The Unity Gateway API for managing model services, model provider services, and MCP services is now generally available, with create, read, update, list, and delete support across Azure Databricks developer tools: Terraform provider: 1.132.0 and later Databricks CLI: v1.17.0 and later Python SDK: databricks-sdk 0.136.0 and later Go SDK: databricks-sdk-go v0.178.0 and later Java SDK: databricks-sdk-java 0.153.0 and later JavaScript SDK: @databricks/sdk-aigateway 0.19.0 and later Declarative Automation Bundles support, through the Databricks CLI 1.17.0 and later, is in Beta. For API documentation, see the Unity Gateway API reference. For examples and tutorials, see the following: Create a custom model service Create and manage providers with Model Provider Services External MCP servers.

summary: You can now use a single VARIANT function to mask columns of type ARRAY and MAP, in addition to STRUCT and other types. This requires Databricks Runtime 19 or above. See Masking multiple column types with a single function.
title: VARIANT cast extends to ARRAY and MAP columns in ABAC column masks

summary: Azure Databricks now automatically deletes a service principal's OAuth client secret after 90 days without use, consistent with unused access token cleanup. If a deleted secret is still needed, create a new OAuth secret.
title: Unused OAuth client secrets are automatically deleted after 90 days

summary: The Unity Gateway API for managing model services, model provider services, and MCP services is now generally available, with create, read, update, list, and delete support across Azure Databricks developer tools: Terraform provider: 1.132.0 and later Databricks CLI: v1.17.0 and later Python SDK: databricks-sdk 0.136.0 and later Go SDK: databricks-sdk-go v0.178.0 and later Java SDK: databricks-sdk-java 0.153.0 and later JavaScript SDK: @databricks/sdk-aigateway 0.19.0 and later Declarative Automation Bundles support, through the Databricks CLI 1.17.0 and later, is in Beta. summary: Managed agent memory and managed agent sessions are in Beta. Azure Databricks now provides two fully managed, Lakebase -backed stores for agent state, both usable from agents built on any framework: Managed agent memory gives agents durable, long-term memory that persists across conversations, with semantic search. See Agent memory. Managed agent sessions store durable conversation history that an agent reads at the start of a turn and appends to as it runs. See Agent sessions.
title: Managed agent memory and sessions are in Beta

summary: Genie One now supports account-only users, so users in a registered identity provider can access account-level Genie One without being assigned to a workspace or granted consumer access. When enabled, eligible users are enrolled automatically. Unity Catalog continues to govern what each user can see. See Account-only user access to Genie One.
title: Account-only user access to Genie One (Beta)

summary: Genie One now supports account-only users, so users in a registered identity provider can access account-level Genie One without being assigned to a workspace or granted consumer access. When enabled, eligible users are enrolled automatically. Unity Catalog continues to govern what each user can see. See Account-only user access to Genie One.
title: Account-only user access to Genie One (Beta)

summary: Starting in October 2026, webhook-triggered deployments for Databricks Apps will be generally available. Automatically deploy your app when changes are pushed to a connected GitHub or Azure DevOps repository, so your deployed app stays in sync with your repository without manual redeployment. See Deploy a Databricks app.
title: Webhook-triggered deployments for Databricks Apps will soon be generally available

summary: Automatic change data feed (Auto CDF) is rolling out to workspaces over the next month and will be available in all supported regions by the end of October 2026. Auto CDF computes row-level changes at query time using row tracking, so you don't need to enable change data feed on each Delta Lake or Apache Iceberg v3 table. It requires Databricks Runtime 19 or above with row tracking enabled. See Automatic change data feed.
title: Automatic change data feed will soon be available in all supported regions

summary: Sharing and reading foreign Delta tables with OpenSharing is now generally available. Providers can share Delta-format tables federated from OneLake, a Hive metastore, or AWS Glue, without copying data into Azure Databricks. See Add foreign Delta tables to a share.
title: Sharing foreign Delta tables with OpenSharing is now generally available

summary: You can now set a maintenance window on a continuous Lakeflow pipeline to control when Azure Databricks applies platform updates that require a restart, such as new runtime versions and serverless infrastructure maintenance. Select a day of the week, a start hour, and a time zone, and Azure Databricks starts maintenance only within that one-hour window. Configure the window in the Jobs UI, the Pipelines UI, or the Jobs REST API. See Manage updates for continuous pipelines.
title: Maintenance windows for continuous pipelines

summary: Data Classification can now scan Unity Catalog views in addition to tables, classifying columns for sensitive data using the same detection engine. This is a Beta feature. See Classify views.
title: Data Classification now scans Unity Catalog views (Beta)

summary: You can now manage Lakebase snapshots programmatically. The snapshots API lets you create, get, list, and delete point-in-time snapshots of a project branch, and restore a snapshot by creating a new branch from it. This API is in Beta and available to all Lakebase workspaces. See Create a snapshot.
title: Lakebase snapshots API (Beta)

summary: Data Classification can now scan Unity Catalog views in addition to tables, classifying columns for sensitive data using the same detection engine. This is a Beta feature. See Classify views.
title: Data Classification now scans Unity Catalog views (Beta)

summary: In early October 2026, running JAR tasks on serverless compute will be automatically enabled for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled. Package your Java or Scala Spark code in a JAR and run it as a JAR task on serverless compute in a Lakeflow Job, without provisioning or managing clusters. See Create and run JARs on serverless compute.
title: JAR tasks on serverless compute will soon be available for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled

summary: Window measures support unitless offset and trailing / leading ranges on a consecutive integer order column. Use a numeric index for non-calendar periods such as fiscal weeks or 4-4-5 periods. See Window measures on a numeric index column.
title: Window measures on a numeric index column in metric views

summary: The counter_diff window function calculates differences between consecutive cumulative counter values and handles counter resets, for time-series analysis of counter data. It is available in Databricks SQL and Databricks Runtime 19 and above. See counter_diff analytic window function.
title: The counter_diff SQL window function is now available

summary: When a Genie response includes a chart, the visualization now appears as an image in the Slack reply. If you installed the Databricks Genie app for Slack previously, reinstall it to enable this. See Visualizations.
title: Genie visualizations in Slack replies (Public Preview)

summary: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is now available on Unity Gateway with text and image inputs. See supported regions. You can access this model using Foundation Model APIs. Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.
title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is now available on Unity Gateway

summary: You can now set performance_target to STANDARD in the Jobs API. Apache Airflow's DatabricksSubmitRunOperator also supports this. See Create and trigger a one-time run and Select a performance mode.
title: Standard performance mode is now available for one-time runs in the Jobs API

summary: Sharing and reading foreign schemas and foreign tables with OpenSharing is now generally available. Providers can share foreign schemas and tables federated from external data sources using Lakehouse Federation, without copying data into Azure Databricks. See Add foreign schemas or tables to a share for providers and Read data in a shared foreign table or foreign schema for recipients. Sharing foreign schemas and tables materializes data on the provider's side, which incurs compute and storage costs. See How do I incur and check OpenSharing costs?.
title: Sharing foreign schemas and tables with OpenSharing is now generally available

summary: Sharing and reading foreign Iceberg tables with OpenSharing is now generally available. Providers can share Iceberg tables federated from foreign Iceberg catalogs using Lakehouse Federation, including to recipients using external Iceberg clients. See Add foreign Iceberg tables to a share for providers and Read data in a shared foreign Iceberg table for recipients.
title: Sharing foreign Iceberg tables with OpenSharing is now generally available

summary: Restore the Python variables and Spark session from a serverless compute job run into a new interactive notebook, so you can debug a failure or explore results without rerunning the entire job. Azure Databricks captures the snapshot automatically for eligible runs. See Session restore for serverless jobs.
title: Session restore for serverless jobs is in Public Preview

summary: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is now available on Unity Gateway with text and image inputs. See supported regions. You can access this model using Foundation Model APIs. Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.
title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is now available on Unity Gateway

summary: The Azure Databricks Excel Add-in is now generally available. Connect Microsoft Excel to your Azure Databricks workspace to browse and import governed Unity Catalog tables and views, run SQL queries, build pivot tables, use custom functions, and write data back to Unity Catalog. You can now also enable Live query when building pivot tables to see results as you update the fields. See Connect to Azure Databricks from Microsoft Excel.
title: The Azure Databricks Excel Add-in is now generally available

summary: You can now create managed tables in Lakeflow pipelines and write to them with one or more append flows. This feature is in Beta. You can also use import_checkpoint on an append flow to migrate an existing Structured Streaming workload into a pipeline without reprocessing the source. See create_table, CREATE TABLE... FLOW (pipelines), and append_flow.
title: Managed tables in Lakeflow pipelines (Beta)

summary: You can now upload PowerPoint (.pptx) files to a Genie One conversation. See Upload a file.
title: PowerPoint uploads

summary: Genie One can now suggest a memory when it detects a fact worth remembering in your request and asks you to confirm before saving it. Approve, modify, or reject the suggestion. See Add to Genie One's memory.
title: Memory confirmation prompts (Beta)

summary: Genie Code skills now appear and are turned on by default in Genie One. Turn individual skills on or off on the customization page.
title: Genie Code skills in Genie One (Beta)

summary: You can now send steering messages to Genie One while it's answering, so you can guide a response without waiting for it to finish.
title: Backend steering

summary: Each Genie Agent supports up to 50 tables, views, or metric views as data sources, up from 30. See Technical requirements and limits.
title: Increased data source limit

summary: Each Genie Agent can store up to 200,000 conversations, up from 10,000. See Technical requirements and limits.
title: Increased conversation limit

summary: Genie One and Genie Code can now use Databricks-provided MCP connectors for Google Drive, Gmail, Google Calendar, Microsoft 365, Atlassian, Slack, and GitHub to search and act on your company's tools while answering questions. Every connection is governed through Unity Catalog and Unity Gateway, which authorizes each tool call, enforces built-in policies and approval requirements, and logs usage and audit activity. Each user authenticates individually, and OAuth tokens aren't shared. See Connect Genie One to external applications with MCP.
title: Databricks-provided MCP connectors for Genie One and Genie Code are generally available

summary: On a published dashboard, the Ask Genie input bar now shows the chart you selected as context, so you can ask questions about that specific chart. See Ask Genie about a specific chart.
title: Selected chart as Ask Genie context

summary: On a published dashboard, Ask Genie's suggested starter questions are now scoped to the dashboard page and widget you're viewing.
title: Scoped starter questions

summary: On a dashboard with relationships, each widget now responds only to filters whose dataset is related to it, so a filter no longer affects unrelated charts. See Dashboard relationships.
title: Relationship-scoped filters (Public Preview)

summary: Path maps can now connect a sequence of ordered points into a line, from separate longitude and latitude columns or a single point geometry column, in addition to a single geometry line column. Use this for trajectories such as GPS tracks. See Path source.
title: Path maps from point sequences

summary: Importing Tableau reports with the /importBI Genie Code command now supports more cases of parameterized calculations. See Import BI files using Genie Code.
title: More Tableau calculations in /importBI

summary: When building a dashboard, Genie Code now prefers governed metric views over ad-hoc SQL datasets and reuses an existing metric view when one satisfies the request. See Use Genie Code for dashboard authoring.
title: Metric view reuse when building

summary: Line and area charts now have a Line shape control that connects data points with linear, smooth, or stepped lines. See Line shape.
title: Line shape control

summary: Key insights now generate for each dashboard page. A New insights badge appears only when new insights are available, along with a live-generating indicator.
title: Key insights per page

summary: You can now export a dashboard's theme to a JSON file and import a theme file into another dashboard, so you can reuse or share a theme without editing the dashboard JSON. See Export or import a theme.
title: Export and import dashboard themes

summary: The pivot table color scale now includes an Apply to setting, so you can paint the color gradient on the cell text as well as the background. See Value-level settings.
title: Color scale on pivot table text

summary: When you export a dashboard dataset as a materialized view in Unity Catalog, you can now choose which SQL warehouse runs the materialization. See Export a dataset as a materialized view.
title: Choose the warehouse for materialization

summary: In early October 2026, horizontal scaling for Databricks Apps will be automatically enabled for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled. Horizontal scaling lets you run an app across multiple instances behind a single app URL for higher availability and concurrency. See Horizontal scaling for Databricks apps.
title: Horizontal scaling for Databricks Apps will soon be available for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled

summary: Genie Code now includes conversation controls that let you branch and revise a chat. You can fork a conversation into a new, independent thread from a point you choose, ask a quick side question with /btw without adding it to the thread, and edit an earlier message to regenerate the conversation from that point. See Branch and edit Genie Code chats.
title: Genie Code adds conversation controls

summary: External secrets connect a Unity Catalog schema to Azure Key Vault. The secrets appear in Unity Catalog as read-only securable objects that you govern with Unity Catalog privileges. Azure Databricks reads their values from Azure Key Vault on demand. See Azure Key Vault secrets in Unity Catalog.
title: External secrets in Unity Catalog (Beta)

summary: Account admins can now set an account-wide retention period from 30 to 3,650 days for supported system tables. See Configure system table data retention.
title: Configurable retention for system tables is in Beta

summary: The Celigo connector is now available in Lakeflow Connect in Beta. Workspace admins can control access to this feature from the Previews page. The connector ingests audit log events, such as create, update, and delete operations on resources, from Celigo (integrator.io) into Azure Databricks. Authentication uses a Celigo integrator.io API token. See Celigo connector.
title: Celigo connector (Beta)

summary: The Anysphere Organization connector is now available in Lakeflow Connect in Beta. Workspace admins can control access to this feature from the Previews page. The connector uses the Anysphere (Cursor) Organization Admin API to ingest organization members, groups, and group members into Azure Databricks as daily snapshots. Authentication uses a Cursor Organization Admin API key. See Anysphere Organization connector.
title: Anysphere Organization connector (Beta)

summary: The Anaplan connector is now available in Lakeflow Connect in Beta. Workspace admins can control access to this feature from the Previews page. The connector ingests audit trail events and user account records from your Anaplan tenant into Azure Databricks. Authentication uses an Anaplan CA certificate and its paired private key. See Anaplan connector.
title: Anaplan connector (Beta)

summary: Databricks SQL version 2026.36 is rolling out to the Current channel. See features in 2026.36.
title: Databricks SQL version 2026.36 is rolling out in Current

summary: Incremental ingestion for Salesforce formula fields in Lakeflow Connect will soon be generally available. Today, Lakeflow Connect ingests formula fields by taking a full snapshot on each pipeline run by default. When incremental formula field ingestion is generally available, full snapshots will no longer be the default. Incremental ingestion typically improves performance and reduces cost. See Ingest Salesforce formula fields incrementally.
title: Incremental ingestion for Salesforce formula fields in Lakeflow Connect will soon be generally available

summary: time_bucket returns the start of the fixed-width interval a timestamp falls into, aligned to an origin you choose (for example, 15-minute or 3-month buckets). Use it instead of date_trunc when the bucket width or start is not a calendar unit. See time_bucket function.
title: time_bucket SQL function aligns timestamps to fixed-width time buckets

summary: You can now turn on the generate_citations option in the ai_search function to see which retrieved chunks the model used to support each answer it generates. ai_search function
title: See which chunks support each ai_search answer (Beta)

summary: ABAC DENY policies are in Beta in Unity Catalog. DENY policies can be used to explicitly deny the MANAGE ACCESS CONTROL privilege to prevent specified principals, including object owners, from performing access-management operations. They always take precedence over any grant. For details, see ABAC DENY policies (Beta).
title: ABAC DENY policies are in Beta

summary: Ingesting into tables backed by default storage with Zerobus Ingest in Lakeflow Connect is now in Public Preview. See Create or identify the target table.
title: Zerobus Ingest into default storage is now in Public Preview

summary: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra is now available on Unity Gateway for enterprise reasoning, structured document processing, coding, agentic search, multimodal inputs, and long-context workloads. You can access this model using Foundation Model APIs pay-per-token. Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.
title: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra is now available on Unity Gateway

summary: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra is now available on Unity Gateway for enterprise reasoning, structured document processing, coding, agentic search, multimodal inputs, and long-context workloads. You can access this model using Foundation Model APIs pay-per-token. Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.
title: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra is now available on Unity Gateway

summary: Currently, the compliance security profile checks and enforces only the use of specific VM instance types, not the enablement of Azure Virtual Network encryption. Enforcement of the Azure Virtual Network encryption requirement begins on June 1, 2027, including on workspaces that already have the compliance security profile enabled. See Compliance security profile and Configure enhanced security and compliance settings.
title: Compliance security profile will enforce Azure Virtual Network encryption

summary: You can now share metric views with Azure Databricks users in other metastores or accounts using OpenSharing. See Add metric views to a share and Read shared metric views.
title: Share metric views with OpenSharing (Beta)

summary: Private network gateway is in Beta. A private network gateway connects Azure Databricks serverless compute to resources in your VNet, on-premises systems, and the internet through a single managed gateway, reusing your existing network connectivity configuration (NCC). Use it for broad private connectivity without onboarding each resource individually, to route serverless egress through your own security appliances for content inspection, or to send egress from a stable set of IP addresses. Account admins can enable it from the account console Previews page. See Private network gateway.
title: Private network gateway is in Beta

summary: You can now select environment version 6 as your base environment for serverless and standard classic compute. See Environment version 6.
title: Environment version 6 is now available

summary: Lakebase is now available in japaneast (Japan East). For the full list of supported regions, see Region availability. To get started, see Get a Postgres database.
title: Lakebase now available in Azure Japan East region (japaneast)

summary: The Genie mobile app can now send push notifications for scheduled tasks to iOS devices. See Push notifications.
title: Push notifications for scheduled tasks (Public Preview)

summary: In embedded dashboards, the Ask Genie button is now hidden when it isn't supported. See Ask Genie in embedded dashboards.
title: Ask Genie button hidden when unsupported

summary: Genie Agents chat mode now uses upgraded large language models.
title: Upgraded chat-mode models

summary: When a SQL function is attached as a tool, you can now view the function's description. See How does Genie use SQL functions?.
title: SQL function descriptions

summary: Dashboard variable options now show their source dataset as a subtitle. See Create a dashboard variable.
title: Source dataset for options

summary: Genie Code no longer appears to stall between edits, and multi-step edits apply with less delay between steps.
title: Smoother editing

summary: You can now apply rich text formatting to dynamic data references in text widgets, widget titles, and descriptions.
title: Rich text for dynamic data references

summary: Importing reports from Power BI and Tableau with the /importBI Genie Code command now includes ranked table calculations.
title: Ranked table calculations in /importBI

summary: Downloads from a metric view now use the display names defined for its fields. See Local metric views.
title: Metric view downloads respect display names

summary: New authoring capabilities and fixes for Genie Code: Improved automatic widget layout: When Genie Code adds widgets to a dashboard, it now places them in available layout space automatically.
title: Genie Code for dashboard authoring

summary: In embedded dashboards, you can now set and retrieve filter values through APIs. See Control dashboard filters programmatically.
title: Embedded dashboard filter APIs

summary: Dashboard subscriptions delivered to Slack and Microsoft Teams can now include data attachments in CSV, TSV, or Excel format. See Data attachments.
title: Data attachments in Slack and Teams

summary: Enhancements to dashboard variables: Multiple fields: Viewers can now add, remove, and swap multiple fields through a dashboard variable on a visualization, instead of switching one field at a time. See Use dashboard variables.
title: Dashboard variable improvements

summary: When datasets are connected by a relationship, filters, selections, and parameters applied to one dataset now automatically carry across to widgets built on the related datasets. See Create dashboard relationships.
title: Cross-dataset filtering through relationships (Public Preview)

summary: In a dashboard's theme settings, you can assign a specific color to a value by name. Any visualization that colors by that value uses the assigned color across the dashboard, for both color by field and color by series. See Consistent colors across widgets.
title: Color mappings

summary: Scrollbars now stay visible on scrollable faceted charts.
title: Always-visible scrollbars on faceted charts

summary: Model Serving now supports Google Gemini 3.8 Flash as a Databricks-hosted model. You can access this model using Foundation Model APIs. Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.
title: Google Gemini 3.8 Flash now available as a Databricks-hosted model

summary: You can now use Shared Serverless to share serverless compute and a pyproject.toml -managed environment across notebooks and files in a Git folder. See Use Shared Serverless for Git folders and bundles.
title: Shared Serverless is in Beta

summary: Model Serving now supports Google Gemini 3.8 Flash as a Databricks-hosted model. You can access this model using Foundation Model APIs. Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.
title: Google Gemini 3.8 Flash now available as a Databricks-hosted model

summary: You can now index and filter struct and map columns in AI Search, and run filter-only queries that return rows matching a filter without vector or keyword retrieval. See Query an AI Search index.
title: AI Search supports struct and map columns and filter-only queries

summary: Unity Gateway now supports Anthropic Claude Fable 5.1 as a Databricks-hosted model. You can access this model using Foundation Model APIs. Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms.
title: Anthropic Claude Fable 5.1 now available as a Databricks-hosted model

summary: SQL and the Scala and Python DataFrame APIs now support variant_strip_nulls, which recursively removes object fields whose values are variant nulls.
title: variant_strip_nulls function

summary: The new parse_sql function parses a SQL statement and returns structured JSON containing statement metadata, table references, select-list expressions, or parser error information.
title: parse_sql function

summary: Data Source v2 JDBC pushdown now emits the SQL NULL literal instead of the string 'null'. Queries that group expressions such as NULLIF now produce a null group instead of a separate 'null' string group.
title: JDBC pushdown correctly handles null literals

summary: http_request and AI functions no longer follow HTTP 3xx redirects. Calls that receive a redirect now return a remote HTTP failure for the redirect status. File-source connector downloads are unaffected.
title: HTTP and AI functions no longer follow redirects

summary: When protobuf schema pruning is enabled, from_protobuf no longer decodes or validates fields that a query does not select. A malformed unselected field no longer nulls the row in PERMISSIVE mode or fails the query in FAILFAST mode.
title: from_protobuf skips malformed unselected fields when schema pruning is enabled

summary: Automatic change data feed (Auto CDF) computes row-level changes at query time using row tracking, without requiring you to manually enable change data feed on each Delta Lake or Apache Iceberg v3 table. Auto CDF removes write-time overhead and makes MERGE and UPDATE operations about 15% faster on tables that you query for changes. It works with batch queries, Structured Streaming, and Delta Sharing, and requires Databricks Runtime 19 or above with row tracking enabled. See Automatic change data feed.
title: Automatic change data feed is generally available

summary: HITRUST and IRAP compliance controls are now generally available through the compliance security profile. In addition, HIPAA, HITRUST, and IRAP now require the compliance security profile. See HITRUST and Infosec Registered Assessors Program (IRAP).
title: HITRUST and IRAP compliance controls are now generally available

summary: Genie Code scheduled tasks are now generally available. You can schedule Genie Code to run a prompt on a recurring schedule. Each run executes your prompt as a full Genie Code session and produces a continuable Genie chat with the results, so you can turn recurring analysis and other work into an unattended background task. Create a scheduled task by asking Genie Code in chat or from the Schedules menu. See Genie Code scheduled tasks.
title: Genie Code scheduled tasks are now generally available

summary: Because SQL statements can contain sensitive information, Azure Databricks now masks query text in the following places: statement_text in system.query.history returns <REDACTED>. query_text in the Query History API and the List Queries API returns <REDACTED>. Keys in request_params in system.access.audit that contain SQL definitions are omitted. Account admins and members of the databricks_pii_access account group can read unmasked query text. To grant access, an account admin creates the group and adds members. See Create and manage the databricks_pii_access group. For details about the masked fields, see Access masked statement text and Access masked request parameters. To read the masked fields from compute that uses dedicated access mode, the compute must run Databricks Runtime 15.4 LTS or above, and the workspace must be enabled for serverless compute. Otherwise, queries fail with an error such as Principal '<principal>' does not have USE SCHEMA on Schema 'system.__internal_functions'. See Fine-grained access control on dedicated compute.

summary: Databricks SQL version 2026.35 is now available in the Preview channel. Review the following section to learn about new features and behavioral changes. Aggregate arrays with collect_union The collect_union aggregate function returns the distinct union of the elements in arrays within each group. HAVING is evaluated before window functions in queries with generators For queries that include generators, such as explode, window functions are now evaluated after the HAVING filter. Window results include only the rows that HAVING retains. Policy logic is hidden in query plans by default Query plans no longer expose row filter and column mask policy logic unless the user has the INSPECT_POLICY_EXECUTION metastore privilege. See Row filters and column masks. CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW preserves metadata atomically For Unity Catalog views, CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW now performs an atomic replacement that preserves the view identity, grants, tags, and comments by default. Governed tag protections continue to apply.
title: Databricks SQL version 2026.35 is now available in Preview

New features is_valid_variant function: The is_valid_variant function returns true if the input is a well-formed VARIANT value and false otherwise. Use it to validate variant data before downstream processing. DataFrameGroupBy.cov and SeriesGroupBy.describe in pandas API on Spark: The pandas API on Spark now supports DataFrameGroupBy.cov, which computes the pairwise covariance of columns within each group, and SeriesGroupBy.describe, which generates descriptive statistics for each group. pa.ChunkedArray support in createDataFrame: createDataFrame() now handles pandas DataFrames with PyArrow ChunkedArray columns, preventing type errors when you use Arrow-backed pandas data.
title: August 17, 2026

summary: Restore the Python variables and Spark session from a serverless compute job run into a new interactive notebook, so you can debug a failure or explore results without rerunning the job. Azure Databricks automatically captures a state snapshot when an eligible run fails, runs 30 minutes or longer, or is cancelled, and keeps it for 7 days after the run completes. This feature is in Beta. See Session restore for serverless jobs.
title: Session restore for serverless jobs is now in Beta

summary: You can now use %uv init, %uv add, and %uv sync in serverless notebooks running environment version 5 or above to create a Python project, add dependencies, and sync its environment. See Create reproducible project environments with %uv.
title: Manage project environments with %uv commands

summary: Identity attributes are in Beta. You can now write Unity Catalog ABAC column mask policy conditions that target users by attributes synced from your identity provider, such as department or country, in addition to group membership. The has_identity_attribute_value and has_identity_attribute_tag_match functions are supported in the WHEN clause of column mask policies. See identity attributes.
title: Identity attributes in ABAC column mask policies (Beta)

summary: The Workiva connector is now available in Lakeflow Connect in Beta. Workspace admins can control access to this feature from the Previews page. The connector ingests audit activity, users, and roles from your Workiva organization into Azure Databricks. Authentication uses Workiva OAuth2 client credentials. See Workiva connector.
title: Workiva connector (Beta)

summary: Sharing managed Iceberg tables in Databricks-to-Databricks sharing and open sharing is now generally available. Providers can now also share managed Iceberg tables to external Iceberg clients. See Add managed Iceberg tables to a share and Read shared managed Iceberg tables.
title: Sharing managed Iceberg tables is now generally available

summary: You can now upload files to Genie Code to use as context for the current chat. See Attach files.
title: Genie Code supports file uploads

summary: Programmatic management of Lakebase Postgres is now generally available through the REST API, Databricks CLI, and Databricks SDKs (Python, Java, Go). These interfaces support operations for projects, branches, endpoints, databases, roles, credentials, synced tables, and catalogs. See Lakebase API guide.

summary: OpenSharing support for tables backed by default storage is generally available and on by default for most accounts. Until it is enabled for your account, an account admin can turn on the OpenSharing for Default Storage – Expanded Access feature from the Previews page in the account console. See Manage Azure Databricks previews.

summary: OpenSharing SecureConnect is generally available. Azure Databricks will make it available by default for accounts on the Premium plan in mid-September 2026, and by early 2027 for the rest. Until it is available for your account, an account admin on the provider side can turn on the OpenSharing SecureConnect preview from the Previews page in the account console. See Share data behind a firewall with SecureConnect and Manage Azure Databricks previews.
title: OpenSharing SecureConnect will be available by default for all accounts

summary: Azure Databricks will be expanding networking billing for OpenSharing SecureConnect. Today, data providers are billed for data transfer (egress) when recipients access shared data through SecureConnect. Additional charge types and access scenarios, including charges billed to recipients, are planned. Azure Databricks does not charge for private connectivity (network connectivity configuration, or NCC) data processing. The following table summarizes the planned charges, who is billed, and how each applies across access scenarios: Charge type Status Cross-region or cross-cloud Same-region (classic or open recipient) Same-region (serverless recipient) Data transfer Available today Bill to provider Not applicable ¹ Not applicable ¹ Public Connectivity Coming soon Bill to recipient Not applicable ² Not applicable ³ ¹ Data transfer (egress) does not apply when the recipient is in the same region as the provider. ² Azure Databricks does not bill this charge. If recipients on classic compute or open recipients reach storage over the public network, their own cloud provider might bill them for network address translation (NAT) directly. ³ Same-region serverless recipients read from storage directly. For rates, see Data transfer and connectivity pricing, or contact your Azure Databricks account team.
title: Expanded networking billing for OpenSharing SecureConnect

summary: Smart Routing (Beta) automatically picks the right model and agent harness for each task, based on complexity, permissions, and budget. It shifts routine work to lower-cost models and reserves frontier models for hard problems, and every routing decision is visible and auditable. Smart Routing works with Claude Code and Codex when you run them through the Unity Gateway CLI or Omnigent, and routes across both proprietary and open models. Only Omnigent can route across coding harnesses, not just models. In internal benchmarks, it matched frontier-level quality while cutting overall task cost by more than 30%. See Select models or use Smart Routing.
title: Smart Routing: Cut AI costs by routing each task to the right model

summary: Google Gemini 3.7 Flash is now available on Unity Gateway for fast, cost-efficient everyday tasks. Access it through the same governed API as other models, with centralized permissions, guardrails, spend controls, and observability, and switch models without changing application code. Customers are responsible for ensuring their compliance with applicable terms. To query the model and see supported regions, see Use foundation models.
title: Google Gemini 3.7 Flash is now available on Unity Gateway

summary: The Sensitive Data Detection guardrail (Beta) detects structured sensitive data (such as Social Security numbers, credit card numbers, IBANs, and phone numbers) and either blocks the interaction or redacts the matched values in place. Detection is deterministic (regular expressions plus checksums and context keywords, with no evaluator model), so it adds under 50 ms for a 100-turn conversation and returns the same result every time. To use it, enable the Enhanced Unity Gateway preview on the account console Previews page. This release also includes the following improvements: Blocked interactions now return a standard HTTP 200 response with the block reason, instead of a 4xx error, so coding agents that resend history don't re-trigger the same block every turn. Built-in LLM-as-a-judge guardrails can now evaluate a window of recent conversation turns, or the entire conversation history, instead of only the latest message. A new execution flow view shows the order in which guardrails run, end to end. See Detect sensitive data with a service policy.
title: Block or redact sensitive data in requests and responses

summary: The Tags page in Governance Hub is now in Beta. The Tags page provides a centralized view of how tags are applied across your account. It summarizes governed tag usage, shows recent tag assignments and their sources, and surfaces recommendations to fix invalid tag values and add tags to important assets that are missing them. Account admins can enable Governance Hub from the account console Previews page. See Tags overview.
title: Tags page in Governance Hub (Beta)

summary: The SQL alert task in Lakeflow Jobs now supports all compliance security profile standards that Azure Databricks supports and is available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled. Use the task to evaluate a Databricks SQL alert as part of a Lakeflow Job. The task returns its evaluation state as a task output value, so downstream tasks can branch on the result. See SQL alert task for jobs.
title: SQL alert task in Lakeflow Jobs is now available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled

Providers can share these tables with any recipient, whether open or Azure Databricks, including recipients that use classic compute. If the feature is not yet on by default for your account, an account admin can enable it in the account console. For more details about the feature, see Limitations and Create shares for OpenSharing. For more details about enablement, see Sharing tables backed by default storage will be enabled by default for all accounts.

Providers can share data from cloud storage behind a firewall or private endpoint without adding each recipient's network to an allowlist, and recipients access the shares using their existing OpenSharing setup. See Share data behind a firewall with SecureConnect and OpenSharing recipient firewall configuration for SecureConnect. SecureConnect is being made available by default for provider accounts on a rolling basis. See OpenSharing SecureConnect will be available by default for all accounts. See Expanded networking billing for OpenSharing SecureConnect.

summary: The SendGrid connector is now available in Lakeflow Connect in Beta. Workspace admins can control access to this feature from the Previews page. The connector ingests the SendGrid subuser directory and IP access-management activity for the parent account and each subuser into Azure Databricks. Authentication uses a SendGrid parent-account API key, with support for both the global and EU data-residency endpoints. See SendGrid connector.

summary: Identity attributes are in Beta. Azure Databricks can store nine IdP-sourced attributes, such as title, department, and cost center, on account users, so they can be referenced in Unity Catalog ABAC column-masking policies. Account admins provision these attributes from their identity provider using automatic identity management or account SCIM 2.1, and use the Identity Attribute Control List to govern which attributes can be written. See Identity attributes.

The connector ingests messages, labels, drafts, filters, and profile data using a Google service account, and syncs the messages and message_labels tables incrementally through the Gmail History API. This feature is in Beta. See Gmail connector.

summary: You can now use the general_access private endpoint to reach Azure Databricks workspaces through inbound Private Link with your custom URL (<my-custom-account-name>.azuredatabricks.net). A single general access endpoint can serve workspaces and account-level resources across regions, and you allowlist registered endpoints through context-based ingress. See Configure inbound Private Link for workspaces.

summary: You can now control serverless network traffic between Azure Databricks workspaces. Account admins use cross-workspace access to set which source workspaces can reach a workspace (ingress) and which destination workspaces a workspace's serverless workloads can send traffic to (egress). Traffic flows only when both the source workspace's egress rules and the destination workspace's ingress rules permit it. See Cross-workspace access.
